# Identity secrets engine - TPM (API)

Vault represents a physical or virtual Trusted Platform Module (TPM) device as a
record in the identity store identified by its Endorsement Key (EK) public key.
TPM records allow Vault to track and control access for specific TPM devices.

Key characteristics of TPM records:

- The **ID** is automatically derived as the SHA-256 hash of the decoded bytes
  from the `tpm_ek_public_key` field and cannot be changed after creation.
- The `tpm_ek_public_key` field is **immutable** and is only set at creation time.
- TPM IDs are scoped to a namespace, so the same EK public key may be
  registered in multiple namespaces without conflict.
- A **disabled** TPM cannot be used for authentication or certificate
  generation.

## Create a TPM

This endpoint creates a new TPM record. The `tpm_ek_public_key` field is
required and must be a PEM-encoded public key with the `PUBLIC KEY` header.
Create a new TPM record from a PEM-encoded public key with the `PUBLIC KEY`
header.

| Method | Path             |
| :----- | :--------------- |
| `POST` | `/identity/tpm`  |

### Parameters

- `name` `(string: "tpm-<random-hex>")` – A human-friendly name for the TPM
  record. The TPM name must be unique within the namespace. If you do not provide
  a name, Vault generates a default name in the format `tpm_<random-hex>`. You
  can update the name later using the update endpoint.

- `tpm_ek_public_key` `(string: <required>)` – PEM-encoded TPM Endorsement Key
  (EK) public key. The key must be a valid PEM block with type `PUBLIC KEY`. The
  key value is **immutable** and cannot be changed after the TPM record is created.

- `metadata` `(key-value-map: {})` – Metadata to be associated with the TPM
  record. In CLI commands, you can repeat the `metadata` parameter multiple
  times and Vault will merge them together to create a single update string.

- `disabled` `(bool: false)` – Whether the TPM is disabled. You cannot generate
  certificates or authenticate with a disabled TPM.

### Sample payload

```json
{
  "name": "my-tpm",
  "tpm_ek_public_key": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMIIBIjANBgkq...\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n",
  "metadata": {
    "machine_name": "server-01",
    "location": "datacenter-east"
  },
  "disabled": false
}
```

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    --request POST \
    --data @payload.json \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/identity/tpm
```

### Sample response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "disabled": false,
    "id": "sha256-a3f1c2d4e5b6...",
    "metadata": {
      "location": "datacenter-east",
      "machine_name": "server-01"
    },
    "name": "my-tpm",
    "tpm_ek_public_key": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMIIBIjANBgkq...\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n"
  }
}
```

## Read TPM by ID

Query a TPM record by its identifier.

| Method | Path                    |
| :----- | :---------------------- |
| `GET`  | `/identity/tpm/id/:id`  |

### Parameters

- `id` `(string: <required>)` – Identifier of the TPM record.

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/identity/tpm/id/sha256-a3f1c2d4e5b6...
```

### Sample response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "disabled": false,
    "id": "sha256-a3f1c2d4e5b6...",
    "metadata": {
      "location": "datacenter-east",
      "machine_name": "server-01"
    },
    "name": "my-tpm",
    "tpm_ek_public_key": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMIIBIjANBgkq...\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n"
  }
}
```

## Update TPM by ID

Update an existing TPM record by its identifier.

The `tpm_ek_public_key` field cannot be changed. Supplying a value that differs
from the existing key returns an error.

| Method | Path                    |
| :----- | :---------------------- |
| `POST` | `/identity/tpm/id/:id`  |

### Parameters

- `id` `(string: <required>)` – Identifier of the TPM record.

- `name` `(string: <optional>)` – Updated name for the TPM record. The new name
  must be unique within the namespace.

- `metadata` `(key-value-map: {})` – Updated metadata. Replaces the existing
  metadata entirely.

- `disabled` `(bool: false)` – Whether the TPM is disabled.

### Sample payload

```json
{
  "name": "renamed-tpm",
  "metadata": {
    "machine_name": "server-01-updated"
  },
  "disabled": true
}
```

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    --request POST \
    --data @payload.json \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/identity/tpm/id/sha256-a3f1c2d4e5b6...
```

### Sample response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "disabled": true,
    "id": "sha256-a3f1c2d4e5b6...",
    "metadata": {
      "machine_name": "server-01-updated"
    },
    "name": "renamed-tpm",
    "tpm_ek_public_key": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMIIBIjANBgkq...\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n"
  }
}
```

## Delete TPM by ID

This endpoint deletes a TPM record by its identifier. Deleting a record that
does not exist is idempotent and returns no error.

| Method   | Path                    |
| :------- | :---------------------- |
| `DELETE` | `/identity/tpm/id/:id`  |

### Parameters

- `id` `(string: <required>)` – Identifier of the TPM record.

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    --request DELETE \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/identity/tpm/id/sha256-a3f1c2d4e5b6...
```

## List TPMs by ID

Fetch a list of all TPM record identifiers in the current namespace.

| Method | Path                          |
| :----- | :---------------------------- |
| `LIST` | `/identity/tpm/id`            |
| `GET`  | `/identity/tpm/id?list=true`  |

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    --request LIST \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/identity/tpm/id
```

### Sample response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "keys": [
      "sha256-a3f1c2d4e5b6...",
      "7d8e9f0a1b2c..."
    ]
  }
}
```

## Create/Update TPM by name

Create or update a TPM record by name. Vault creates a new record if no TPM with
the given name exists and the `tpm_ek_public_key` is set. Otherwise, Vault
updates the record with the given name, if it exists.

| Method | Path                        |
| :----- | :-------------------------- |
| `POST` | `/identity/tpm/name/:name`  |

### Parameters

- `name` `(string: <required>)` – Name of the TPM record.

- `tpm_ek_public_key` `(string: <required on create>)` – PEM-encoded TPM
  Endorsement Key public key. Vault requires the key when creating a new record.
  You cannot change the key on an existing record.

- `metadata` `(key-value-map: {})` – Metadata to be associated with the TPM
  record. Replaces the existing metadata entirely on update.

- `disabled` `(bool: false)` – Whether the TPM is disabled.

### Sample payload

```json
{
  "tpm_ek_public_key": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMIIBIjANBgkq...\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n",
  "metadata": {
    "machine_name": "server-02"
  }
}
```

### Sample request

```shell-session
$ curl \
    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    --request POST \
    --data @payload.json \
    ${VAULT_ADDR}/v1/identity/tpm/name/my-tpm
```

### Sample response

```json
{
  "data": {
    "disabled": false,
    "id": "sha256-a3f1c2d4e5b6...",
    "metadata": {
      "machine_name": "server-02"
    },
    "name": "my-tpm",
    "tpm_ek_public_key": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\nMIIBIjANBgkq...\n-----END PUBLIC KEY-----\n"
  }
}
```

## Delete TPM by name

Delete a TPM record by its name. Deleting a record that does not exist is
idempotent and returns successfully as a no-op.

| Method   | Path                        |
| :------- | :-------------------------- |
| `DELETE` | `/identity/tpm/name/:name`  |

### Parameters

- `name` `(string: <required>)` – Name of the TPM record.

### Sample request

```shell-session

    --header "X-Vault-Token: ${VAULT_TOKEN}" \
    --request DELETE \
```
